P03-023.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.17.11 opens on the word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.17.11), and its near face is licensed by that formula alone. The cut is declined on the stated ground that one word-event unit runs from the formula at 17:11 to the signature at 17:21 and that the verdict completes the indictment rather than opening a fresh address; the alternative is recorded as paragraph-grade and held.
P03-023.device_notes: The verses of this span carry no paseq and no editorial note (single witness). P10-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:48, one of the counted transport verses (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ (oshb:Ezek.40.48) “he brought me to the porch of the house” (web:Ezek.40.48), marking entry into the temple building proper, distinct from every court and gate measured before it. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.41.1) “He brought me to the nave and measured” (web:Ezek.41.1), disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) “He said to me,” then “This is the most holy place” (web:Ezek.41.4), the guide's naming of the room, which closes the survey of it by reading; the he-said-to-me that naming carries is an onset-type device inside the vision and not a close formula; 41:5's fresh measuring verb then turns to a new object, the house wall. This close therefore rests on a reading of the guide's speech and not on a counted close-role formula.
P10-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Leaving 40:48-49 as its own two-verse row was rejected as a two-verse fragment; splitting porch from nave at 41:1 was also weighed, since 41:1's transport verb is itself a counted guided-motion verse, but no close-grade device stands between 40:49 and 41:1 to justify the cut, whereas 41:4 supplies the guide's naming.

P10-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens on a said-to-me verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י, and then carries בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) stands inside 43:19, embedded between the relative clause about the priests near to me and the infinitive that follows it, so it closes nothing there, neither a paragraph nor the row, and the seven-day consecration instructions run on. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) “Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord Yahweh” (web:Ezek.43.27), this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses), single witness -- the close rests first on that verse-final utterance formula, with the doubled mark standing behind it as corroboration. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

P11-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.5 opens with a son-of-man address launching an instructional mode; 44.6 and 44.9 both carry the messenger formula, addressed throughout to the same topic (the house of Israel's abominations in admitting uncircumcised foreigners to the sanctuary) with no addressee-class change between them, so neither reopens the row on its own. The unit turns at 44.10 to the Levites' judgment for their prior idolatry: they may minister but may not approach as priests, with the utterance signature appearing mid-paragraph at 44.12 (paragraph-final, not row-final, since no fresh onset follows immediately) and the paragraph closing at 44.14. Close: Ezek.44.14 closes on content — the Levites set as keepers of the house's charge — with no close-role formula of its own, and the pe parashah mark recorded after Ezek.44.14 (single-witness) corroborates that close without supplying one, so that near face is the ground on which this row is held at reduced confidence; the very next verse, 44.15, turns to a different priestly class (the sons of Zadok) with its own utterance signature standing verse-final at its end -- an addressee-class shift inside the same law section.
P11-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 44.9/44.10 (foreigner law versus the Levites' judgment), since 44.9 is itself a messenger-formula restatement. Weighed on both faces: the near face, Ezek.44.10, opens the Levites' judgment with no onset formula of its own, and the far face, Ezek.44.9, restates the messenger formula without ending on a close-role formula, so the rival is unlicensed on the face that would carry it. Rejected because no addressee-class change occurs there -- both halves concern the same reform of sanctuary access -- and no parashah or refrain marks that point, while the pe after 44.14 (single witness) corroborates this row's own close instead.
